How to Read Scene Focus Before Writing Visual Prompts

Scene Focus tells the creator what the viewer should notice or feel before the Image Prompt supplies the full visual instruction.

Topic
Visual Planning
Best for
Creators using Kyunolab script packages
Read time
3 min read
Updated
Jul 18, 2026
Advertisement

Scene Focus is the intention

Scene Focus is not a short version of the prompt. It explains the role of the image in the viewer's experience.

It may point to doubt, isolation, discovery, danger, or a small detail that changes the meaning of the Scene.

Image Prompts translate that intention

The Image Prompt turns the focus into a concrete scene. It describes space, subject, light, mood, color, camera feeling, and realism.

Reading Scene Focus first helps the creator judge whether the generated image supports the story instead of only looking attractive.

Use Focus to reject the wrong image

A generated image can be technically good and still wrong for the Scene. If it misses the Scene Focus, it should be revised.

The question is not only whether the image looks mysterious. The question is whether it makes the viewer understand the right moment.

Keep the visual choice specific

Strong mystery visuals usually depend on one clear subject. A crowded image can weaken the story because the viewer does not know where to look.

Scene Focus helps narrow the image before the prompt expands it.
